newsitem.title: USA: Burlington sees cost-cut payoff in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Burlington sees cost-cut payoff in 1998.

text.p: Burlington Industries Inc said Monday it expects its efforts to improve profitability will increase its earnings starting in 1998.

In a statement announcing the company's third quarter results, Burlington chief executive George Henderson said, "At the present time, we are taking a number of cost cutting actions to improve our profitability."
"While these moves penalize current earnings, we are confident that they will have a positive impact in 1998 and beyond," he said.
Burlington reported third quarter net income of $13.5 million or $0.22 per share, compared with $0.6 million or $0.01 per share a year earlier.
The 1997 results reflected a net $7.7 million or $0.13 per share after-tax charge for one-time streamlining costs.

The 1996 results reflected an after tax charge of $20.3 million or $0.33 per share to close Burlington's Knitted Fabrics division and an after-tax provision of $4.7 million or $0.07 per share for legal contingencies and asset sale losses.
Henderson said the company's third quarter results were in line with its expectations, adding business generally remains firm and Burlington saw improvement in its denim business.
